key_insight: PI-GMDH builds the solution structure progressively, using physics- and data-informed criteria to add functional terms only where they improve the coupled Navier-Stokes representation.
engineering_relevance: For fluid mechanics problems, this adaptive construction can reduce model size and training cost while preserving high accuracy on incompressible flow fields.
method: Evaluate candidate basis directions via the first variation of the full physical + observational objective.
Add functions progressively and optimize coefficients with block-coordinate damped Gauss-Newton.
Demonstrate the approach with tensor-product Chebyshev expansions on the 2D time-dependent Taylor-Green vortex.
evidence_signal: On the benchmark test, adaptive PI-GMDH achieved validation and held-out test losses of 5.299e-19 and 5.296e-19, with 204, 201, and 175 active functions for u, v, and p.
watch_item: The reported advantage is benchmark-specific, so the structural-construction policy may not generalize without tuning for harder or noisy CFD data.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Method of Group Data Handling: Adaptive Construction of Functional Representations with an Application to the Navier-Stokes Equations
